items.title: The actual exact-gradient Picard phase and its first-order difference

source.attribution: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang; scoped actual Lemma4.6 numerical-kernel interface, explicit normalized-curvature boundary and universal constant elaboration.

items.statement: At this explicit normalized C2 curvature interface, the actual exact-gradient two-Picard map Phi is measurable and defines a Markov kernel K(z)=Gamma.map(Phi_z). For every synchronously coupled input pair and every two-vector noise value, the actual integral average H is symmetric, (2kappa)^-1 I<=H<=I and ||H||op<=1. There exists a genuine continuous real linear R on the L2 phase space such that Delta1=Delta0+h*(Delta p,-H Delta x-Delta p)+R Delta0 and ||R||op<=8 Lambda h^2. R may depend on z,zprime,zeta; no measurable choice or global derivative of Phi is asserted. H, Phi, K and the remainder are constructed, not supplied as conclusion certificates.
assumptions: E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space, including dimension zero, with its Borel measurable space. f:E->R is globally C2. kappa>=1 and every genuine nested second derivative satisfies (2kappa)^-1||v||^2 <= D2f(z)[v,v] <= ||v||^2 for every z,v. These are the normalized smoothed-potential curvature interface; f=V_eta and Lemma4.1 are independent prerequisites.

J>=2,h>0. The nodes are t_j=h/2(1-cos(j*pi/(J-1))), ell_j their actual Lagrange cardinal polynomials, Lambda=sup_{s in[0,h]} sum_j|ell_j(s)|, omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i}(t_i-s)ell_j(s)ds, b_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s)ds and c_j=integral_0^h(h-s)ell_j(s)ds. Assume only h^2 Lambda<=1. In particular h<=1 is derived, never added as a premise.

a=exp(-h/2),sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)),Gamma=stdGaussian(E) product stdGaussian(E). Both Gaussian vectors are independent under Gamma and shared synchronously between compared inputs. P0=a p+sigma zeta0; Y0_j=x+t_j P0; Y1_i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij gradient f(Y0_j); Phi=(x+hP0-sum_j c_j gradient f(Y1_j),a(P0-sum_j b_j gradient f(Y1_j))+sigma zeta1). No stochastic gradient/proximal array appears.

For every pair z,zprime and every Gaussian vector zeta (not just almost surely), H_j is the ordinary Bochner integral of the Riesz-represented genuine D2f along the Y1prime_j-to-Y1_j segment; H=h^-1 sum_j b_j H_j. The source phase norm is the Euclidean L2 product WithLp2, not the default product max norm.

formulae.label: Actual first-order difference, explicit constant
formulae.tex: \Delta_1=\Delta_0+h(\Delta p,-H\Delta x-\Delta p)+\mathcal R_h\Delta_0,\quad\|\mathcal R_h\|_{\rm op}\le8\Lambda_Jh^2,\quad\frac1{2\kappa}I\preceq H\preceq I.

obligations.label: Actual two-Gaussian exact-gradient kernel, source integral-averaged H and L2 remainder bound at exposed normalized curvature

bindings.boundary: This is the actual deterministic numerical kernel/first-order difference interface in Lemma4.6, conditional on the explicitly exposed normalized C2 curvature producer. The identity f=V_eta and source Lemma4.1 smoothing/curvature production remain open. It does not prove Proposition4.7 contraction/step absorption, Lemma4.8 M_kappa increment, logarithmic Lambda/B2, Khat/Kbar accuracy, invariance, repeated-history/cost, PBPS, either complete main theorem or their actual-input expected-cost composition. Khat and Kbar cannot be replaced by this K; TV closeness cannot transfer unbounded cost.
